\par\smallskip
\begin{minipage}{\textwidth}\footnotesize
Note: Native Methods = methods declared native (JNI and JNA direct mapping) + JNA interface and dynamic bindings + JNR-FFI and FFM bindings. The breakdown rows count resolved natives and add up to SysJava Resolved; Platform / Intrinsic = natives and bindings for other operating systems (Windows, macOS, Solaris, BSD), JVM intrinsics, and bindings with no native target (FFM upcall callbacks, vDSO calls). Not Found = natives with no symbol in any available library, and JNA/FFI bindings whose library or symbol is unknown. SysJava Resolved + Platform / Intrinsic + Not Found = Native Methods. Tomcat 11 uses the FFM API extensively (382 FFI bindings), reflecting the move away from JNI in newer Java versions; FFM hits that the detector inferred from a class name in a JAR that never references java.lang.foreign (e.g. clojure.core\$abs, EvpHmac\$MD5) are not counted. JNA and FFI bindings are resolved statically using SysJava's binding rules and constant propagation to API arguments. Solr and Storm include natives mapped by supplying the library the image does not ship (Solr netty-tcnative 2.0.70: 276; Storm jansi: 9 and netty io_uring: 62, which adds io\_uring\_setup/enter/register; Tomcat: 2 commons-daemon natives in jsvc, built from the image's commons-daemon-native source; OrientDB jffi 1.3.11: 37 and Lucene NativePosixUtil: 5; Elasticsearch NativePosixUtil: 5). Unanalysed Lib Syscalls ($\Delta$) are syscalls reachable from native libraries present in the container but without a direct Java binding entry point, not already counted above; the Go Whitelist ($\Delta$) adds the runc entries not already counted. All ten containers run under their generated profiles.
\end{minipage}
